newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO warns of deeper crisis before Netanyahu visit.
newsitem.headline: PLO warns of deeper crisis before Netanyahu visit.

text.p: On the eve of a trip by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Washington to discuss the disintegrating peace process, Palestinians warned on Saturday of a "comprehensive explosion" that could increase confrontations.
The warning followed more than two weeks of clashes between Israeli troops and Palestinian protesters over a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"The powers of peace are being rejected and the powers of violence are being pushed forward," said Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary-general of the Palestinian cabinet.

Netanyahu, invited to a crisis meeting with President Bill Clinton at the White House on Monday, offered on Friday to hold intensive three-way talks with U.S. and Palestinian leaders on a final peace deal if there is no progress after six months of further talks.
In Tel Aviv on Saturday, preparations were underway for a peace rally later in the day.

"We are calling on our leader (Netanyahu) and all of the leaders in the region and around the world to join together to save the peace process," Oren Yehishalom, one of the rally's organisers, told Reuters.

Abdel-Rahman said the Palestinian cabinet decided on Friday to send an urgent message to Clinton to "explain the seriousness of the current situation which could lead to confrontations". He did not say how or when the message would be delivered.

"The current situation could lead to a comprehensive explosion resulting from the great Israeli pressures on our people in the security, military, economic and humanitarian spheres," a Palestinian cabinet statement said.
David Bar-Illan, Netanyahu's communications director, said such statements would not promote peace.

"It's regrettable that the language of threats and violence has now entered the vocabulary of Palestinian Authority leaders as Netanyahu is going to Washington to try to put peace talks back on track."
Bar-Illan said Netanyahu will relay to the Americans his demand that the Palestinian Authority crack down on "terrorism" as a condition for resuming peace talks.
Israel has charged that the Palestinians gave a green light for the resumption of suicide bombings by Moslem militants after a year-long lull.

Palestinians, who blame the unrest on Israel actions, says peace talks can restart only when Israel halts work on the new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
But Netanyahu vowed in advance of his trip to Washington that work at the site, and Jewish settlement of other occupied Arab land, will continue.
Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its capital. The PLO wants East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967, as capital of a future Palestinian state.

Palestinians sees fresh Jewish settlement construction as an effort to pre-empt the negotiations they are supposed to hold on the future of East Jerusalem and the rest of the West Bank under agreements signed by the previous Israeli government.
